title: Control Plane — Stitchwork & Sprintlight weekly bridge notes (2026-11-19)
content:
Purpose
Quick weekly bridge for the control-plane + routing/auth/quotas slice — catch up on work in flight, surfaced risks, and short tactical decisions. Focus this week: finishing the small-fallthrough revert path, quota edgecase test harness, and auth token cache eviction tuning experiment.

Attendees (live): Aisha, Marco, Priya, Tomoko, Ethan (+ async notes from SRE rotation)

High-level takeaways
- Small-fallthrough rollback is staged on canary; we observed reduced tail latency but increased ops noise. Decision: keep canary for 48h, limit the rollout to 10% until quota tests clear. (owner: Marco)
- Quota edgecases: batch of customer reports indicate incorrect remaining_quota when requests retried across regions. Root cause suspected: race between quota-check and routing-fanout for multi-shard requests. Short-term mitigation drafted (see action items). (owner: Priya)
- Auth cache tuning: Tomoko's eviction policy (LRU with TTL bump on validate) looks promising — needs load test with long-lived sessions. (owner: Tomoko)

Metrics snapshot (last 72 hours) — pulled by Ethan from observability playbook
- Controlplane median p95 propagate time: 28ms -> 26ms after optimization; p99 improved 5% on canary nodes.
- Average quota-check latency: 12ms but a bimodal tail at ~840ms when quota service downstream throttles.
- Auth validation hit ratio: 82% on default 10m TTL; expected to hit 90% with new policy.
- Canaries that saw small-fallthrough revert: 17% fewer 500s but +2 ops incidents (manual restarts) — investigating restart trigger.

Notes and discussion items
1) Small-fallthrough revert path (Marco)
- What we did: introduced a lighter-weight fallback that falls through to the next compatible model rather than immediate error. Canary showed improved user visible latency but edge cases where request context was lost during model swap.
- Next: add request-id preservation through the fallthrough boundary; add test that replays multi-step chat sessions across fallthroughs. Jira: PLT-2748.
- Open question: should model-variant fallback preserve client-specified routing hints (region, dedupe key)? If not, we should annotate those requests and fall back to strict routing — consistency vs availability tradeoff. (tl;dr: prefer preserving routing hints for enterprise customers, relax for public tiers).

2) Quota checks and retry race (Priya)
- Repro notes: retried requests sometimes hit different quota shards; quota service uses eventual propagation window of ~200ms which is insufficient for high-retry workloads.
- Proposed quick mitigation: on retry, attach original-quota-check token and prefer the original shard if available. Implemented as a routing flag that pins shard for 1s after initial check. Prototype is in branch: allocator/quota-pin-proto.
- Longer term: move to strongly consistent quota-metadata writes for cross-shard ops or a single-shard reservation for batched requests. This is higher effort (infra + DB changes).

3) Auth token cache eviction experiment (Tomoko)
- Problem: bursty traffic creates auth validation storms hitting identity provider.
- Experiment plan: bump TTL to 30m for tokens validated more than 3 times in a 10m window, and implement LRU eviction plus gentle TTL decay. Load test schedule: Friday 11/20 in staging with synthetic 10k concurrent clients.
- Success metric: reduce calls to idp by >=50% without increasing auth-related 401s above baseline.

4) Routing: regional fallback & prioritization (Aisha)
- Quick note: routing policy update rolled to bikeshed that gives priority to in-region pools and then to low-cost out-of-region. We need to ensure quota checks do not double-count when we perform cross-region fallback. Adding a guard in router: only perform cross-region fallback if target pool has free quota-bucket. (owner: Aisha)

5) Incident retrospective snippet (E-2 on 2026-11-12)
- Cause: simultaneous controlplane leader elections during a config rollout caused transient quorum loss, which increased request timeouts and surfaced quota-check failures. Action: staggered rollout window + leader election backoff tuned. PR: github.com/redwood-inference/controlplane/pull/998.

Action items (concrete, prioritized)
- Marco: extend canary window to 48h and add request-id preservation layer in fallthrough handler. See PLT-2748. (due 2026-11-21)
- Priya: land quota-pin prototype for retries and add unit+integration tests that simulate cross-shard retries. Include mitigation toggle. (due 2026-11-24)
- Tomoko: run auth cache load test in staging (11/20), collect metrics, iterate on TTL thresholds. (due 2026-11-20)
- Ethan: add an observability panel for "quota retry divergence" (visualize shard-mismatch events) and alert if >1% of retried requests land on different shards. (due 2026-11-22)
- Aisha: update router to check target-pool quota before cross-region fallback, then run canary. Also draft customer-facing note for enterprise customers about routing hint guarantees. (due 2026-11-23)
- SRE rotation (oncall): add a playbook snippet for manual fallback disable if canary restarts spike. (due 2026-11-21)

Parking lot / research notes (low effort spikes)
- Evaluate using causal-consistent cache for quota tokens to avoid reorder. Short spike: 2d research for cost/benefit. (owner: Priya)
- Prototype retention of routing-hint metadata in the request envelope to survive model-variant swaps. (owner: Marco/Tomoko)

Risks and blockers
- Rolling revert may surface more restarts if underlying vmem leak is present — need deeper heap profiling on canary nodes. Blocker until we can prove restarts are not correlated with fallthrough code. (investigating: Ethan)
- Cross-shard quota correctness: if we cannot pin shards reliably, customers with synchronous retries will have incorrect billing/limits — critical for enterprise. Prioritize mitigations.

Meeting notes style / misc
- Many notes are still WIP; keep this doc as the ground-truth for the week. If you add comments, prefix with initials and date (e.g., "MP 11/18: added repro steps").
- Quick references: Slack thread #pltfm-routing "retry-shard-oddities"; Confluence draft: kv-cache-proposal (link above).

Next meeting agenda (2026-11-24 weekly bridge) -- quick hits
- Canary outcomes (small-fallthrough) + restart correlation
- Quota-pin integration tests results
- Auth cache load test metrics + go/no-go for TTL change
- Any urgent customer escalations re: quotas or routing

Raw scratch / notes to self
- Confirm canary nodes run kernel 6.1.x vs 5.15 in prod — kernel differences might explain restart behavior.
- Add sample replay request for canary test (chat multi-turn) into PLT-2748 test harness.

Files & refs (local branches / PRs)
- allocator/quota-pin-proto (branch)
- controlplane/fallthrough-requestid (branch)
- github.com/redwood-inference/allocator/pull/523 (recent perf tweak landed)

If anything here looks off, ping me (Aisha) in Slack or leave inline comments in this doc.

-- end of notes
